info.title: DCRS API for the Mitra mobile app (the Audit Assistant)
info.summary: Read and change DCRS data as a signed-in person, through DCRS's own rules.
info.description: The Digital Controlled Record System's API for another server acting as a signed-in person (REQUIREMENTS §83). Sign in with POST /api/auth/login; send the session token (the dcrs_session cookie's value) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every /api/v1 call, and name the calling server in `X-Client-Name`. Everything is JSON except the PDF. The person's departments decide what may be read and changed, exactly as in DCRS itself. A session lasts until the close of the day it was started — the end of the plant's working hours (6:20 pm unless the super admin changes them) for everybody but the super admin, whose session lasts until midnight, factory time (REQUIREMENTS §84); `session.endsAt` in the sign-in answer says when. Outside the plant's working hours — before the opening, after the close, on the weekly off or a festival holiday — anybody but the super admin is refused with 403 `outside-working-hours`. WHAT MITRA DOES, FROM THE MOBILE APP (REQUIREMENTS §85): the routes tagged Mitra — documents, today's facts, records found, read, searched and printed, records opened, changed and acted on, the equipment list (F/MNT/01) and what stands out (the insights) — are answered by DCRS's own engine run on the server, so every change goes through DCRS's own checks, history and activity log, exactly as Mitra's own tools in the browser; each one maps to one of Mitra's tools (docs/chatbot-integration.md has the table). The super admin's escalations (GET /api/v1/escalations) are read from the server's own, for the super admin only. A CHANGE must be confirmed by the person first. See docs/chatbot-integration.md.

post.summary: Sign in as a person (DCRS's own sign-in)
post.description: The session token is the value of the `dcrs_session` cookie in the `Set-Cookie` header of the answer. It lasts until the close of the day it was started — the end of the plant's working hours for everybody but the super admin, midnight (factory time) for the super admin — and `session.endsAt` says when. Send it back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or as the cookie). Outside the plant's working hours anybody but the super admin is refused with 403 `outside-working-hours`, after the password was found right. Eight wrong passwords for one email in 10 minutes are refused with 429 for the rest of those 10 minutes.

post.summary: CHANGE — close a finding with a note
post.description: Exactly what DCRS's own Close button does: the finding becomes Closed with today's date (the factory's) as its date of action, and the report is saved as the page saves it (a report still Due becomes In Progress; any other keeps its status). The report's history gets an entry in the person's name with the note "Through <X-Client-Name>: <note>", and DCRS's activity log gets a "Record edited" line saying the same. Refused when the finding is already closed, when its report is verified (reopen it in DCRS with Edit first) or sent back (Resume it in DCRS first).

post.summary: CHANGE — change a record with Mitra's patch (Mitra's edit_open_record)
post.description: The patch is applied by DCRS's own engine exactly as Mitra applies it (engine/recordPatch.ts): every field checked against the form, every value normalised to what the form stores, printed and computed columns never written, one line changed only when the match names exactly one. The change is saved as the record's page saves it (a Due record becomes In Progress, computed cells worked out), with its own entry in the record's history — in the person's name, the note "Through <client>: <note>" — and the activity line "Record edited through Mitra" with the same words. What was left out is in `problems`; a patch that changes nothing is 400 nothing-changed. A record that is not open for writing (submitted, verified, sent back) is 409 needs-reopen: reopen it with a reason first (POST .../actions reopen). Ask the person first.

post.summary: CHANGE — submit, verify, send back, resume, reopen, cancel a correction, delete (Mitra's record_action)
post.description: What the record page's buttons do, through DCRS's own lifecycle and validation (engine/recordLifecycle.ts): submit (a record being filled in; DCRS's validation must pass, 409 invalid with the problems otherwise), verify or approve (a submitted record; a complaint checklist's approval stamps Approved By), send_back with a reason (a submitted record), resume (one sent back), reopen with a reason (submitted, verified or sent back — it must then be submitted and verified again), cancel_correction (puts a reopened record back exactly as it was), delete with a reason (recorded on the deletions log). Each writes its entry in the record's history in the person's name with the note "Through <client>: <reason or the action>", and the activity line the browser writes for it (Record submitted for verification, Record verified, Record sent back, Record resumed, Record reopened for correction, Correction cancelled, Record deleted) with the detail "Through <client>: …". Ask the person first.

post.description: For a record with a photo list (the complaint acknowledgement) or a scan list (the service agreement): the picture is added as Mitra adds one, with its own history entry "Through <client>: photo <fileName> added" (or the note). get.summary: READ — a machine on the equipment list, F/MNT/01 (what Mitra answers about a machine)
get.description: The machines on F/MNT/01, the List of Equipments & Utilities, that `q` names: a Machine No. (M-47, m47, machine no. 47), a serial number, a model or a maker (Delta 330, Brison), a place (QC, Lombardi Printing), or the person's question as they asked it. `answer` is Mitra's own reply to those words, as her rules path gives it in DCRS (engine/equipmentMasterAssistant.ts), and null when they are not a question she answers there. `machines` are the machines the words name by number, or the one a serial only it has names (`exact`); otherwise, when Mitra has no answer of her own, the machines DCRS's own search finds for the words. A model name never picks one machine, because the list repeats its model names. A line F/MNT/01 prints one column out of step (M-68) is read back in step, and says so in `note`. Without `q`: the list itself — how many machines, their numbers and the numbers it skips. The list is Maintenance's: anybody else is refused 403 not-your-department.

From.description: The first date, YYYY-MM-DD (today and yesterday are read too).

NotSignedIn.description: No session, a session whose day has closed (a session ends at the close of the day it was started: the end of the working hours, or midnight for the super admin), or an account switched off. Sign in again.

value.error: Not signed in, or the session has ended. Sign in again with POST /api/auth/login.

PasswordChangeRequired.description: The account is still on the password the administrator gave it (password-change-required): the person must sign in to DCRS in a browser and choose their own. Or it is outside the plant's working hours (outside-working-hours) — refused to everybody but the super admin; `opensAt` says when DCRS opens again.

value.error: This account is still on the password the administrator gave it. Sign in to DCRS in a browser and choose your own first.
DCRS is open 8:40 am to 6:20 pm on working days. Today is Thursday, the weekly off — it opens again on Friday 2 October at 8:40 am.

NotYourDepartment.description: The person's departments do not include the one that owns these records (not-your-department). Also, as on every /api/v1 route: outside-working-hours outside the plant's working hours, and password-change-required.

value.error: The CAPA findings belong to Quality Assurance, and this account is not kept to it.
DCRS is open 8:40 am to 6:20 pm on working days. Today is Thursday, the weekly off — it opens again on Friday 2 October at 8:40 am.

BadRequest.description: A query value is not one this route accepts.

value.error: status must be "open", "closed" or "all".

BadDate.description: The date is missing or not a real date written YYYY-MM-DD.

value.error: date must be a date written YYYY-MM-DD.

NoReport.description: DCRS holds no live F/HR/17 record for that date.

value.error: There is no daily pest control report (F/HR/17) in DCRS for 2026-09-28.

EngineUnavailable.description: DCRS's engine is not running on the server (engine-unavailable: it is being bundled, or could not be) or failed on this request (engine-failed). Try again in a moment.

value.error: DCRS cannot work this out just now: its engine is not running on the server. Try again in a minute.

RecordNotFound.description: No such record (not-found), or it is another department's (403 not-your-department).

value.error: There is no record "rec-nothing" in DCRS.

ChangeRefused.description: Refused by DCRS's own rules. needs-reopen: the record is submitted or verified — reopen it with a reason first (action reopen). wrong-status: that action does not apply to it now (`actions` says what does). invalid: DCRS's validation stopped it (`problems`). busy: the records kept changing while this was saved — try again.

value.error: the Adhesive Mixing Ratio Record of 30-Sep-2026 is Pending Verification and cannot be changed as it stands. Reopen it for correction first, with a reason (action "reopen"); it will then need submitting and verifying again.
the Adhesive Mixing Ratio Record of 30-Sep-2026 is Pending Verification: only a record being filled in can be submitted.
Submitting it cannot be done yet: 09:00: Viscosity (20.0 ± 1.0 Sec.) is required. 09:00: Tested By is required.
The records kept changing while this was being saved. Try again in a moment.

Error.description: Every refusal. `error` is a sentence to show a person; `code` is for the program. A refusal outside the plant's working hours also says when DCRS opens again (`opensAt`).

opensAt.description: Only with the code `outside-working-hours`: the next moment DCRS opens (the start of the next working day), or null when the plant's calendar has no working day in the year ahead.

id.description: The account's stable id. Never changes; keep it as the person's id in the other system.

role.description: admin is the super admin (every department).

departments.description: Department codes (QA, HR, MKT ...). An empty list means every department.

features.description: What this DCRS server has switched on.

mustChangePassword.description: True: the person must choose their own password in DCRS before the API will serve them (403 password-change-required).

FindingStatus.description: Closed or Verified as stored; otherwise Overdue when the target date is before the factory's today and no date of action is filled in; otherwise Open.

Finding.description: One internal CAPA finding (a line of a Pest Control Inspection Findings Report, owned by Quality Assurance).

id.description: Readable id: CAPA-<report date, with b, c ... for a second or third report that day>-<number>, and .2, .3 for a repeated number. Accepted in any case.

ref.description: Stable reference <record id>:<finding id>. Never changes; accepted wherever an id is.

number.description: The finding's S.No, or its place in the report when it has none.

actionDate.description: The date the action was taken (set by a close).

reportStatus.description: The report's own status in DCRS (Due, In Progress, Pending Verification, Verified, Rejected ...).

total.description: How many match, before limit and offset.

note.description: How the finding was resolved. Kept in the report's history.

Complaint.description: One customer complaint (CAPA — External: Customer Complaint Handling Checklist, F/MKT/05, owned by Marketing).

answer.description: Yes, No, a number (check point 4), or null when not answered.

PestSummary.description: The Daily Pest Control Monitoring Record (F/HR/17) of one date, as data.

status.description: The record's status in DCRS. Due or Scheduled means nobody has filled it in yet.

SessionEnd.description: When this session ends (REQUIREMENTS §84): at the close of the day it was started. Keep `endsAt` as the assistant's own session expiry.

endsAt.description: The end of today's working hours for anybody but the super admin; midnight, factory time, for the super admin (and for everybody on a server that does not enforce the hours). The dcrs_session cookie's Max-Age runs to the same moment; after it every /api/v1 call answers 401 not-signed-in.

signOutAtEnd.description: True for an account held to the plant's working hours: DCRS's own pages warn ten minutes before `endsAt` and sign the person out at it.

PlantHours.description: The plant's working hours and where today stands — the plant's, nothing about any person.

enforced.description: False on a server started with DCRS_WORKING_HOURS=off: nobody is held to the hours.

timeZone.description: The factory's time zone, such as Asia/Kolkata.

hoursText.description: The hours in words: "DCRS is open 8:40 am to 6:20 pm on working days."

DocumentBrief.description: One document (a controlled format). `route` is its page in DCRS and `link` opens it.

kind.description: log-sheet, daily-pest-monitoring, fly-catcher, service-report, gap-inspection, training-record, complaint-checklist, complaint-ack, service-agreement, pest-responsibilities, or a reference kind.

referenceOnly.description: Kept as issued: no records to fill.

documents.description: The person's own documents that match (all of them when there is no q), best first.

kept.description: Another department's documents that match: found, never opened (REQUIREMENTS §84).

notInDcrs.description: Lines of the Master List of Formats (F/SYS/02) that match and DCRS does not hold yet.

Layout.description: What the form is made of, in the keys a patch names. A log sheet: `header`, `footer` (boxes) and `columns`, each {key, label, type, options?, required?, unit?, min?, max?, printed?, computed?, readFrom?}, and `rows` {mode: timeSlots|fixedRows|free|single, slotKey?, slots?, count?}. F/HR/17: `checkpoints` {number, question, answer, noteAsks?, findingWhen?}, `fields`, `lists`. Any other form: `fields` {key, label, type, items?, parts?}. A printed or computed column, or one read from another document (readFrom), cannot be written.

patchShape.description: How a change to this kind of form is written (POST /api/v1/records/{id}/changes).

DueItem.description: One record due, overdue, coming, or waiting. `recordId` is null (and `started` false) for a sheet the calendar has not stored yet: POST /api/v1/records {documentId, date} starts it.

problems.description: needsInput only: what still stops a submit.

Today.description: Mitra's todays_facts: the plant's day and what is due for this person (their departments' documents).

upcoming.description: Due in the next three days.

readyToSubmit.description: Prepared by the assistant and passing validation.

facts.description: The same facts in words, as Mitra is given them.

recordId.description: Null for a sheet the calendar has not stored yet (started: false).

snippet.description: Search only: the words around what was found.

kind.description: register: only a format number was given, so its latest records are listed.

note.description: For a change through an app: "Through <X-Client-Name>: <note or the action>".

RecordDetail.description: Mitra's get_record and get_open_record in one: the record, whether it can be changed now and what can be done to it, its layout (the keys a patch names), its data in words and as stored, and its history (the last 50 entries).

editable.description: Its data can be changed now (Scheduled, Due or In Progress). Otherwise a change needs `reopen` first.

actions.description: What POST .../actions can do to it now.

correction.description: Set while it is reopened for correction: reason, by, at, fromStatus.

prepared.description: Filled by the assistant: at, notes (what to check), basedOn.

photos.description: Which picture list it has, if any (POST .../photos).

linked.description: F/MNT/03 only: the Actual dates read from each machine's F/MNT/02 (not stored on the sheet).

documentId.description: The document's id or its format number.

date.description: The record's date; today (the server's) when left out.

created.description: True when this call stored the record (201); false when it was already on file (200).

patch.description: Mitra's patch (engine/recordPatch.ts applyAssistantPatch). A field: {"<key>": value}. A log sheet: {"header": {"<box key>": value}, "itemEdits": [{"collection": "rows", "match": {"<slot key>": "10:00"} or {"row": 2}, "set": {"<column key>": value}}]}, or "rows" given in full. F/HR/17: {"checkpoints": {"<n>": value or {value, note}}}. Values are read as the form stores them ("yes" -> Yes, "9.15 am" -> 09:15, "20.4" -> 20.4, a select's option however it is cased); a field the form does not have, a printed or computed column, or a value it cannot hold is left out and said in `problems`.

note.description: Why, in the person's words: the history says "Through <client>: <note>".

problems.description: What was left out, and why.

action.description: approve is verify (a complaint checklist's approval stamps Approved By).

reason.description: Needed for send_back, reopen and delete.

dataBase64.description: The picture's bytes in base64 (a data: prefix is allowed), at most 512 KB decoded. DCRS keeps photos scaled to at most 1024 px on the longer side, as JPEG at 70% — scale before sending, as the server does not.

evidence.description: One fact per line, records tagged [rec:<id>] — what Mitra's model is given to answer from.

Machine.description: One line of F/MNT/01 as Mitra reads it: put back in step where the list prints it one column out (then `note` says so), and the list's "NA" and "-" as null.

machineNo.description: M-47: the machine is its number.

section.description: The list's own "Department" column: a section of the plant (Flexo, Common), not one of DCRS's departments.

summary.description: Number, what it is, model, where it stands.

note.description: Only for a line the list prints one column out of step: what was done, and to confirm it against the plate.

list.description: F/MNT/01 itself: the record the machines are read from, how many there are, their numbers and the numbers it skips.

answer.description: Mitra's own reply to the words, as her rules path gives it in DCRS; null when they are not a question she answers there.

exact.description: The Machine No. the words name without doubt: a number, or a serial only one machine has.

rule.description: Which insight rule found it (A1, B2, M6, …).

evidence.description: Up to five of the records it was read from, newest first.

headline.description: The line Mitra is given with every message in DCRS: the counts by severity and the most severe titles.

period.description: The ISO week it belongs to, such as 2026-W40.

summary.description: The line Mitra adds for the super admin in DCRS, or that nothing is waiting.

waiting.description: How many are not yet acknowledged.
